6.11.19 Graduate Study for Faculty. Ordinarily, faculty members may become candidates for graduate degrees at this institution only if they hold the rank of instructor, with inherent rights of attaining salary increments, tenure, and promotion. Faculty members of higher rank than instructor are encouraged to attain advanced degrees and continue study at other institutions. However, faculty members of higher rank than that of instructor shall have this privilege under the following specific conditions: #21-22-6, #21-22-43
a. The program to which the faculty member applies for matriculation has not been identified by the Dean of the Graduate School as oversubscribed. #21-22-43
b. Taking the degree represents retraining or adding competence and enhancing the faculty member’s contribution to the institution rather than serving to qualify the person for initial appointment to the General Faculty. Although this option may be used for the retraining and redirecting of faculty, the entry into matriculation for a degree shall not constitute a presumption of eligibility for another position at the University. #20-21-36

c. Unless specific, alternate arrangements are made, no released time from teaching, scholarship, or service shall be part of the decision to accept a faculty member’s application for matriculation. #21-22-6
d. Permission to apply for matriculation shall be obtained in advance from the faculty member’s department chair, the dean of the college in which the faculty member holds rank and the Vice Provost for Graduate Education,Research and Outreach (for those wishing to pursue a graduate degree). After that step, ordinary procedures for processing applications will apply.
6.11.20 Teaching Excellence. All teaching faculty are expected to strive for and maintain the highest standards of excellence in teaching effectiveness as set forth in the guidelines adopted by the Faculty Senate.

6.12.10 The Students. Students seeking knowledge and understanding also need freedom to inquire, to conduct research and to exchange ideas through discussion, publication and such public presentations as in the fine arts. These opportunities are basic to education in and for a democratic society. The former Rhode Island Board of Trustees therefore declared that students in the institutions under its control should have freedom both of inquiry and of expression. In exercising such freedom and in discharging the rights and obligations of citizenship, students must also recognize their responsibilities to other individuals, to the University, to the state and the nation, and to society in general. Orderly and dignified expression and conduct are expected.
6.12.11 The University of Rhode Island, under the jurisdiction of its Board of Trustees, shall adopt specific regulations stating in detail the meaning of this general principle for their respective campuses. #21-22-6 #22-23-25
6.12.12 To illustrate and amplify this statement, yet without restricting its meaning in any respect, the following more specific statements were made by the former Rhode Island Board of Trustees.

6.12.13 Students shall be free to organize and join associations for educational, political, social, religious or cultural purposes. The fact of affiliation with any extra-mural association or national organization or political party, so long as it is an open affiliation, shall not in itself bar a group from recognition as a legitimate campus organization or from use of University facilities. However, no body of students shall organize and act as representatives of the University in outside activities unless approved and authorized by University authorities.
6.12.14 The student government, student organizations and individual students shall be free to discuss any matters that affect them directly or indirectly as students or as citizens, to pass resolutions upon them, to circulate petitions, to distribute leaflets and to take other lawful action respecting them. Orderly demonstrations on campus are permitted.
6.12.15 The principle of freedom of the press is fully applicable to all student publications. The University shall refrain from acts of censorship contrary to this principle.

6.12.16 Visual presentation of information and ideas through the movies, the drama, the dance, painting, sculpture and other art form shall be as free from restraint as the presentation of ideas and information by means of speech or the printed page.
6.12.17 Student organizations on the campus may freely select persons they wish to invite as guest speakers for their programs (see 6.14.10-17).
6.12.18 A student organization, not curriculum-connected, shall be free to choose its own faculty adviser. The adviser shall consult with and advise the organization but shall have no authority or responsibility to regulate or control its activities unless such authority and responsibility are specifically stated and mutually agreed upon in advance.
6.12.19 No disciplinary action shall be taken by the University against a student for engaging in such off-campus activities as political campaigning, or participating in public demonstrations, provided the student does not claim without authority to speak or act in the name of the University or one of its organizations.

6.12.20 The University shall endeavor to develop in its students the realization that all citizens not only have the right but the obligation to inform themselves about problems and issues of concern to the community and the nation. It shall encourage students to formulate points of view regarding these issues and to give expression to them.
6.12.21 The University maintains student records primarily for educational purposes, although student records are maintained for other purposes such as health and employment. Procedures for the release and disclosure of student records maintained by the University are in large measure governed by State and Federal laws. Guidelines incorporating the requirements of the Federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974 are published annually in the student handbook.

6.13.10 Speakers on Campus. Students and faculty alike may freely select the persons they wish to invite to the campuses of their respective institutions as guest speakers other than those imposed by state and national law. Obviously, invitations to speakers do not imply approval or sponsorship of their views by the University or college or the URI Board of Trustees, nor necessarily by the organization or person inviting them. Both students and faculty possess the same rights as other citizens to hear different points of view and to draw their own conclusions. #21-22-6 #January 27, 2022 Informational Report
6.14.10 Controversial Persons. The following guidelines govern visits to the campus by controversial persons.

6.14.11 In all circumstances, the civil rights and liberties of every person involved shall be fully respected and protected from any abridgement whatsoever. There shall be no infringement upon the right of speakers to present their views or of visitors to perform their intended service or the right of members of the University community to hear the presentation or benefit from the performance of the intended service or the right of any persons to conduct orderly picketing or make other lawful forms of protest. #21-22-6
6.14.12 Routine procedures required by the University in connection with the appearance of a guest speaker shall be designed only to ensure that there is orderly scheduling of facilities and adequate preparation for the event, and that the affair is conducted in a manner appropriate to an academic community. University control of campus facilities shall not be used as a device of censorship.

6.14.13 When it is known that a potentially controversial person is expected on the campus, with the likelihood of generating some form of protest or demonstration, the President of the University or a designated presidential representative shall make every effort to arrange prior discussions with the probable protesting group or groups. The only purpose of such meetings shall be to establish mutually agreeable arrangements. In no case shall such discussion be construed as implying university endorsement of the protestors’ position. #21-22-6
6.14.14 If a formal protest or demonstration is held, it shall not be confined to a specified area, but persons, or signs or other devices used to express the protest shall not block sight, hearing, access or egress, or otherwise interfere with the orderly conduct of the event being protested or of normal University activities. In order to attain the latter objective, certain areas in which protest activity is to be prohibited may be defined in advance by mutual agreement between the University and the protesting parties.

6.14.15 In the event of a visit to the University by a highly placed government official or a highly controversial person, special arrangements for the visit may be required. Any such arrangements shall be made by the University. Special rules and procedures shall be devised and promulgated by a special University committee representing the University administration (including the campus police forces), the faculty and the student body. Representatives of outside agencies may be invited either to advise or to serve upon the committee. In all such cases, the University shall maintain final control over arrangements, consistent with University rules and regulations.

6.14.16 If any special rules are adopted, they shall be given wide publicity well before the event to which they apply. It is expected that every person on the campus shall act in a lawful manner and observe general and special University regulations. The Vice President for Student Affairs or designated representative shall be present at all occasions when controversy is likely to arise and shall request persons acting in an unseemly manner to desist from such action. Members of the campus community are subject to the disciplinary procedures stated in 9.20.10 and 7.41.10-11 .
6.14.17 The campus police shall normally handle such routine matters as traffic regulations in accordance with established procedures, and whatever problems arise from action in contravention of previously announced policies. In the event of violence, or of clear, unmistakable indication of probable violence, the responsible University official in attendance may authorize a call for additional assistance.
6.20.10 Policy on Religious Observance. No faculty or staff member, administrator or student shall be discriminated against because of religious beliefs or practice.

6.20.11 To facilitate course planning, the University Chaplains shall prepare and provide to staff and faculty a comprehensive listing of religious holy days that traditionally have precluded secular activity. This list shall be provided each semester at least one week prior to the first day of classes. See sections 8.51.11-14 for relevant university make-up policy.
6.30.10 Policy Statement on the Use of Drugs on Campus. The University of Rhode Island asserts its commitment to promoting a drug-free environment. The University’s commitment applies broadly to all segments of the campus community: faculty, staff, administrators, and students alike. #21-22-43
6.30.11 With respect to controlled substances, The University of Rhode island affirms its commitment to enforcement of federal and state statutes restricting the use of such substances as well as the regulations of the University itself pertaining to controlled substances.

6.30.12 With respect to alcohol and tobacco, The University of Rhode Island recognizes the extreme health costs associated with the use of these substances and its responsibility to provide a positive model for young people who are in the process of consolidating attitudes and behaviors that will serve them, positively or adversely, throughout their lives. The University therefore asserts its commitment to enforce fully regulations pertaining to the illegal use of alcohol and drugs and to a program of active discouragement of the use of tobacco and the abuse of alcohol.
6.30.13 With respect to performance-enhancing drugs, The University of Rhode Island strictly prohibits the use of drugs banned by the NCAA by members of athletic teams or individuals representing the University at athletic events. The Department of Athletics shall present and discuss the institutional policies with all athletes participating on intercollegiate sports teams. Student athletes will be required to sign the Awareness Statement Concerning Use of Drugs by Student Athletes.

6.40.10 Accommodations for Qualified Students with Disabilities. All programs, activities and facilities of the University, when viewed in their entirety, must be accessible to qualified students. The Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion in the Dean of Students Office is responsible for determining students’ eligibility for physical accommodations and, in cooperation with the appropriate academic deans, department chairpersons and faculty members, the selection of reasonable alternative means to satisfy the academic requirements of courses and programs of study. Student requests for accommodations are made via the Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion to the University member responsible for the program or activity. Such requests shall be made by the student himself/herself, a parent, legal guardian or other representative. For further information, a regularly updated document titled Policies and Procedures: Academic & Administrative Accommodations for Students with Disabilities, is available through the Office of Disability, Access and Inclusion. #21-22-43

6.40.11 Faculty shall make reasonable efforts to provide alternative means for qualified disabled students to fulfill course requirements. Academic Deans, in consultation with program directors and department chairs, shall modify academic requirements on a case by case basis to afford disabled students an equal opportunity. Academic requirements which the University determines and can demonstrate are essential cannot be modified.
6.40.12 The student with a disability shall be responsible for self-identification to the Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion in the Dean of Students Office, providing appropriate documentation of disability, requesting accommodation in a timely manner, and follow-through regarding accommodations requested. #21-22-43
6.40.13 University members shall use reasonable efforts to ensure confidentiality regarding student information related to a disability in accordance with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act.

6.40.20 Appeal of Accommodation Decisions. A University member or student may request a review of an accommodation decision. The request for reconsideration is to be submitted to the Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion, who shall forward the request to the appropriate Vice President or the Provost for final determination. #21-22-43
6.40.21 The Provost or appropriate Vice President shall review the information received, request additional information if necessary, and make a final decision. The Provost or Vice President shall transmit a decision to the student, the University member and the Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion. #21-22-43
Chapter 11 – University Manual

11.10.10 Changes to the University Manual may be made through legislative action of the Faculty Senate and in accordance with the Constitution and By-laws of the Faculty Senate. Final action by the Senate on a proposal to change the Manual shall not be taken unless the proposal appears on the agenda for the meeting. A proposal which appears on the agenda may be amended from the floor and final action on the amended version may be taken at that meeting. Proposed changes to the University Manual deemed editorial by the Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee will be provided as a report to the Faculty Senate and will require
no action. Following the report, any Faculty Senator may move that a proposed change should be considered substantive. This motion, when seconded, will then be considered for a vote, and if passed, the matter shall be handled as a substantive change and will follow University Manual legislative procedures. #13-14–13 #21-22-10
11.10.11 Changes to the University Manual may also be made by the President in those areas corresponding to presidential responsibility and authority. #13-14–13, #21-22-6

11.10.12 The Coordinator, Faculty Senate, shall be the editor of the University Manual; shall assist the Constitution, By-laws, and University Manual Committee with properly incorporating all changes; maintain an accurate current electronic copy of the University Manual on the Faculty Senate website; and maintain, on the Faculty Senate website, a page or pages with superseded University Manual, constitution, and by-laws sections, with indications when and how they were superseded. #00-01–30 , #13-14–13
11.10.13 University Manual changes based on Faculty Senate action. Following necessary approval of Senate action, University Manual changes shall be submitted to the Chair of the Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee for editorial review, to ensure that they are consistent with the style, format, and arrangement of the University Manual (By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.25 ). Following that review, the Coordinator, Faculty Senate, shall incorporate them into the electronic copy of the University Manual. #13-14–13

11.10.14 University Manual changes based on presidential action. University administrators shall make themselves aware of University Manual passages concerning the units for which they are responsible. Whenever there are changes with respect to their units making modifications of Manual passages necessary, the appropriate administrator shall amend them and submit them to the President for review. The President may appoint a person to assist with that review, but no administrative changes may be incorporated into the Manual without the President having “signed off’ on them. When the President approves of a change, it shall be submitted to the Constitution, By-laws and University Manual Committee for incorporation into the Manual. The Committee shall determine if the proposed changes are in the area of Presidential or Senate authority and shall ensure that the changes are consistent with the style, format and arrangement of the University Manual (By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.25). If the President and Constitution, By-laws and University Manual Committee are not in agreement as to the delegation of authority, the matter shall be referred to the Executive Committee of the Senate. If the changes proposed are deemed to fall under presidential authority, they shall be referred to the Coordinator, Faculty Senate, for incorporation into the electronic copy of the University Manual. #13-14–13, #21-22-6

11.10.15 Information about changes. Following incorporation of changes into the electronic copy of the University Manual, the reference numbers of sections changed, added, or eliminated shall be listed on the next possible Faculty Senate agenda under “Reports of Officers and Executive Committee” for changes resulting from Senate action, under “Report of the President” for changes based on presidential action. #13-14–13
11.10.16 A University Manual maintenance schedule shall be posted on the Faculty Senate website to facilitate identifying responsible parties of each chapter or section of the Manual and the date informational reports or legislative action will be requested. #21-22-40

11.10.17 Editorial changes to the University Manual are defined as and limited to changes required by developments in legal statutes or Collective Bargaining Agreements. Whenever a determination is made that editorial changes to a chapter or section of the University Manual are required outside the ordinary maintenance schedule established in Section 11.10.16, based on developments in law or a Collective Bargaining Agreement, the interested party shall notify the Faculty Senate President and the Faculty Senate Coordinator by providing a detailed justification for the request. The Faculty Senate President will review the request with the Faculty Senate Executive Committee at their next regularly scheduled meeting or refer the request directly to the Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee (CBUM). Upon referral from the Faculty Senate President, CBUM members will review the proposal at their next regularly scheduled meeting or at a special meeting convened sooner than the next regularly scheduled meeting, formulate a recommendation regarding approval, and present the change request along with their recommendation in a report at the next regularly scheduled meeting

of the Faculty Senate.
Consistent with Section 11.10.10 of the University Manual, changes to the University Manual deemed not editorial by CBUM and/or the Faculty Senate shall be made through legislative action of the Faculty Senate or through Presidential action, and in accordance with the Constitution and By-Laws of the Faculty Senate and with Sections 11.10.11, 11.10.12, 11.10.13 , and 11.10.14 of the University Manual. #22-23-16

Chapter 2 – University Manual

2.10.10 Channel of Authority between the University and the Board of Trustees. The normal channel of authority from the URI Board of Trustees to the faculty, administration and staff of the University shall be through the President. All faculty members and administrative and other officers shall be responsible, through appropriate channels, to the President and only through the President to the URI Board of Trustees. #21-22-6 #January 27, 2022 Informational Report #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.11 Administrative Staff of the University shall comprise all full-time employees who are neither in the state classified service nor members of the faculty. This does not include those persons whose appointments are “for one year only” or “to complete current year only.” #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.12 Officers of the University. The officers of the University shall be the President, the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs, the Vice President for Administration and Finance, the Vice President for Research and Economic Development, and the Vice President and General Counsel. Administrative Report September 2015 #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.20 The President is the chief executive officer of the University and in addition to any powers granted by law or regulation, the President shall have full power and authority to manage the institution in a manner consistent with its mission, Strategic Plan, and policies established by the Board of Trustees. The President shall report to the Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.20.21 Succession. In the case of death, termination, resignation, or disability of the President, the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs shall serve as Interim President until another interim or permanent replacement is appointed by the Board of Trustees. #January 27, 2022 Informational Report #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.30 The Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs is the chief academic officer of the University and is responsible for academic programs and faculty actions. The Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs shall have primary responsibility for academic planning, budget development and management, and promotion and tenure procedures for faculty members. They shall act as chairperson of the Council of Deans (Deans’ Council, see 5.12.10-5.12.11 ) and respond to faculty needs for appeals beyond the Deans’ level. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.31 The Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs shall report to the President and serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council. They shall act as Chief Executive Officer of the University in the absence of the President. The Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs shall serve as the primary University liaison to the Academic Affairs and Research Committee of the URI Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.40 The Vice President for Research & Economic Development shall serve as the Chief Research Officer of the University with overall supervision for the research and economic development missions of the University. They are responsible for facilitating ongoing academic research opportunities, strengthening research infrastructure, nurturing research ideas and initiatives, promoting diversity in the University’s research enterprises, and providing a compelling voice for the University’s research activities to both internal and external constituencies. They shall oversee the University’s intellectual property, technology transfer, and serve as an ex officio member of the URI Research Foundation’s Board of Directors. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.41 The Vice President for Research and Economic Development shall report to the President and the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs, serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council, and act as Chief Executive Officer of the University in the absence of both the President and the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs. They shall serve as University liaison to the Academic Affairs and Research Committee of the URI Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.50 The Vice President for Administration and Finance is the chief financial officer of the University and is responsible for financial and business affairs and the physical and technological infrastructure. They shall report to the President, be a member of the President’s Executive Council, and shall serve as the Chief Executive Officer of the University in the absence of the President, the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs, and the Vice President for Research and Economic Development. The Vice President shall serve as the primary University liaison to the Finance and Facilities Committee and the Institutional Risk and Compliance Committee of the Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.60 The Vice President and General Counsel is the chief legal officer of the University and advises the URI Board of Trustees and the University President about the laws, rules and regulations affecting the University. They shall provide legal services to the President and their staff, represent the President and the University before boards, commissions, and courts as necessary, and such other duties as the President may assign. They shall report to the President, be a member of the President’s Executive Council, and serve as the primary University liaison to the Governance Committee of the URI Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.70 President’s Executive Council : The President’s Executive Council shall advise the President on the operations of the University and fulfillment of the University’s mission. It shall consist of the University officers and of the following:

2.10.71 Vice President for Communications and Marketing shall oversee the Office of External Relations and Communications and provide strategic leadership for the development and implementation of the University’s comprehensive marketing and communication strategies that engage the URI’s many audiences and advance the University’s reputation locally, nationally, and internationally. They shall oversee media relations, internal and external communications, crisis communications, marketing, branding, licensing, and digital strategy for the University. They shall report to the President and serve as the President’s chief communication advisor and as a member of the President’s Executive Council. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.72 Vice President for Community, Equity, and Diversity shall lead the University’s effort to develop and sustain a vibrant and diverse community of students, staff, and faculty throughout the University; ensure that community, equity, and diversity are integrated into the University’s core mission, vision, and strategies; advise and inform the President on all issues related to community, equity, and diversity. They shall oversee the Gender and Sexuality Center, the Multicultural Student Services Center, the Women’s Center, the Center for Military and Veteran Education, and the University Diversity Council. The Vice President shall report to the President and serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.73 Vice President for Advancement and CEO of the URI Foundation shall be responsible to the University President and the Foundation’s Board of Directors, and shall conduct the business of the Foundation, including development and endowment management operations. They shall serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.74 Vice President and Director of Athletics shall be responsible for the oversight of the University’s Division 1 intercollegiate athletics, including its varsity sports teams, full time coaches and staff, and student athletes. They shall report to the President and serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council. They shall serve as a University liaison to the Student Life and Athletics Committee of the URI Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.75 Vice President for Human Resources is the principal steward of the human capital and workplace effectiveness at the University, providing strategic leadership and oversight of talent management, including recruitment, learning and development, compensation and classification, policy development and compliance, employee relations and engagement, Human Resources information systems and analytics, and benefits and rewards. The Vice President shall report to the President and serve as member of the President’s Executive Council. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.10.76 Vice President for Student Affairs shall be responsible for providing vision and leadership, strategic direction, policy development and administrative oversight of the Division of Student Affairs, including student services and auxiliary units, ensuring alignment with institutional strategic goals. The Vice President shall report to the President and serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council and as the primary University liaison to the Student Life and Athletics Committee of the URI Board of Trustees. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.10.77 President’s Senior Advisor and Chief of Staff shall be responsible for the overall management of the Office of the President. They shall report and provide executive level support to the President and serve as a member of the President’s Executive Council. They shall also serve as liaison for the President to other members of the President’s Executive Council, the URI Foundation, and the URI Board of Trustees, and shall have administrative oversight of the Office of the Ombuds. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.30.10 Office of the Provost: In carrying out their responsibilities, the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs shall be assisted by the following:
2.30.11 Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success shall report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and oversee enrollment planning, recruitment, admission, new student transitions, academic support programs, and retention for the University’s undergraduate programs and collaborate with enrollment planning and strategy at the graduate level. They shall oversee the Office for Strategic Initiatives, Winter and J-Term, and URI Online, and in collaboration with Student Affairs, support student success programs and services. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.30.12 Vice Provost and Dean of the Graduate School shall report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and serves as the strategic leader and advocate for graduate education at the University. They oversee all aspects of the Graduate School’s operations and work closely with the colleges and schools on graduate enrollment and program development. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.30.13 Vice Provost for Academic and Faculty Initiatives shall report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and assist with all matters of academic administration, policy, planning, and initiatives. The Vice Provost is responsible for program review and accreditation, leading promotion and tenure, and serves as liaison between the University faculty and the Office of the Provost, including with the Faculty Senate. They shall oversee the Office for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning and the Honors Program. They shall serve as the primary representative of the Office of the Provost in the absence of the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs. The Faculty Senate shall appoint at least one representative to the VPAFI search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.30.14 Vice Provost for Academic Resource Management shall report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and provide leadership and guidance with respect to strategic resource planning across the Division of Academic Affairs, including budget management, academic personnel and labor relations, and academic space allocation. They shall work in close coordination with the Office of Financial Strategy and Planning and with the colleges and schools. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.30.15 Vice Provost for Global Initiatives shall report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and serve as the university’s senior international officer. They shall be responsible for the University’s global education strategies, programs, and partnerships. They shall ensure compliance with all federal and state statutes pertaining to the university’s international engagement and with international risk management policies and procedures in collaboration with the University’s risk management office and Office of General Counsel. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.30.16 Provost’s Senior Advisor and Chief of Staff shall report and provide executive level support to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs. They shall serve as liaison for the Provost to the Deans of the Colleges and Schools and shall be responsible for the overall management of the Office of the Provost. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.40.10 Academic Deans report to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and provide overall leadership for their respective college or school, including academic program excellence, and oversight of administration, budget and financial planning, personnel, and strategic planning. (see 3.20.10 – 3.20.11 for duties) The Academic Deans include:
Dean, College of Arts and Sciences
Dean, College of Business
Dean, College of Education
Dean, College of Engineering
Dean, College of the Environment and Life Sciences
Dean, College of Health Sciences
Dean, College of Nursing
Dean, College of Pharmacy
Dean, Graduate School of Oceanography #25-26-Presidential-01

2.40.11 The University Librarian reports to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and is responsible for the overall leadership of the University libraries, including oversight of administration, budget and financial planning, personnel, and strategic planning, and ensuring the provision of services in support of the academic and research missions of the University and in support of faculty and students. (see 3.42.10) #25-26-Presidential-01
2.50.10 The Office of Institutional Research is responsible for the collection, organization, analysis and reporting of institutional and other data to support URI management, operations, strategic decision-making, and planning activities. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.60.10 Associate Vice President for Financial Strategy and Planning shall report jointly to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and the Vice President for Administration and Finance. The Associate Vice President is the leader of Financial Strategy and Planning and responsible for managing the University’s available financial resources efficiently and effectively, and for providing guidance to facilitate operational decision-making and long-term financial planning. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.60.11 Chief Information Officer and Associate Vice President for Information Technology shall report jointly to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and the Vice President for Administration and Finance. The Chief Information Officer is the leader for technology across the University, responsible for planning, coordination, and leadership for the university information technology services and support, including Management Information Services, Technical and Operational Services, Information and Instructional Technology Services, Networking and Telecommunication Services. The Faculty Senate shall appoint at least one representative to the CIO/AVPIT search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01
2.70.10 Appointment of Administrative Officers: The President is appointed by the URI Board of Trustees. Whenever an administrative officer position becomes vacant, there will be a search conducted by the department or division. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.70.11 University Officers and Vice Presidents: Whenever a University Officer, other than the President, or vice president position becomes vacant, the President shall appoint a search committee of at least five members. In addition, the search committee shall include two faculty members appointed by the Faculty Senate. The search committee shall assemble a suitable list of candidates from the applicant pool, screen the candidates by reviewing their qualifications, and make recommendations regarding the candidates to the President. Appointment shall be made by the President from the list of candidates put forward by the search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.70.12 Vice Provosts, Associate and Assistant Vice Presidents, Associate and Assistant Vice Provosts: Whenever one of these positions becomes vacant, the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs or Vice President who oversees the position shall appoint a search committee, which shall include a minimum of five members and shall include staff and faculty representation, and students where appropriate. The search committee shall assemble a suitable list of candidates from the applicant pool, screen the candidates by reviewing their qualifications, and make recommendations regarding the candidates to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs or Vice President. Appointment shall be made by the Provost or Vice President from the list of candidates put forward by the search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.70.13 College or School Deans and University Librarian: Whenever one of these positions becomes vacant, the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs shall appoint a search committee, which shall be chaired by the Provost or an academic dean and be comprised of at least five members who are representative of the faculty of the unit. Each search committee shall also include appropriate staff and student representation. The Faculty Senate shall appoint two members to the search committee. The search committee shall assemble a suitable list of candidates from the applicant pool, which shall include qualified internal candidates if they have applied, screen the candidates by reviewing their qualifications, and make recommendations regarding the candidates to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs. Appointment shall be made by the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs from the list of candidates put forward by the search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01

2.70.14 Associate Deans and Assistant Deans of Colleges or Schools: Whenever one of these positions becomes vacant, the Dean of the College shall appoint a search committee. The search committee shall be comprised of at least five members who are representative of the faculty of the College or School. Each search committee shall also include appropriate staff and student representation. The search committee shall assemble a suitable list of candidates from the applicant pool, which shall include qualified internal candidates if they have applied, screen the candidates by reviewing their qualifications, and make recommendations regarding the candidates to the Dean of the College or School. Appointment shall be made by the Dean from the list of candidates put forward by the search committee. #25-26-Presidential-01

4.10.10 On Faculty Governance. Faculty participation in the government of the University of Rhode Island is essential to its sound development and to the successful performance of its role in the life of the state. The basic functions of the University — teaching and research — are performed by a community of scholars who must exercise sound judgment in the planning and execution of their assigned responsibilities. Since decisions on all academic levels may affect profoundly the performance of all faculty members, provision must be made to ensure that their points of view will be represented in the formulation of policies that control their professional activities. The collective judgment of the scholars who comprise the faculty is a resource of great value which, properly utilized, will help to guarantee that University policy will be wisely established and effectively carried out. #21-22-6

4.11.10 Membership in the General Faculty shall be based on appointment by the President and on direct participation in or supervision of any of the following activities: teaching, librarianship, and research and creative activities, within the University. General Faculty includes those appointed to full-time tenure-track and non tenure-track positions. The President, the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs, the Vice President for Research and Economic Development, the Vice Provost(s), the academic dean and associate dean(s) of each college or school and of the library are also part of the General Faculty. #20-21-25

4.11.11 Any person who has General Faculty status and has assumed responsibility as assistant or associate dean at the University shall retain all voting privileges as a member of a department, college and of the General Faculty. In accordance with Article III of the Faculty Senate Constitution, such persons shall be counted for Senate apportionment proportionate to their percentage of full-time equivalent faculty responsibilities, but may not be elected to the Faculty Senate or participate in Senate elections ( see also section 2.1 of the By-Laws of the Faculty Senate). #20-21-36
4.11.12 Any person who has General Faculty status and is head of an academic program or research unit (e.g. Honors Program, Faculty Institute on Writing, Center for Vector-Borne Diseases, etc.) has all of the voting rights of a full-time member of the General Faculty, including eligibility for election to the Faculty Senate and participation in Senate elections. #20-21-36 #24-25-20

4.11.13 Any person who has had General Faculty status and who is transferred in the University to a position or office which in itself does not carry such status shall retain faculty status so long as that person is employed by the University. However, that person shall not have rank, voting privileges in department or college meetings on matters requiring Faculty Senate approval, tenure (unless earned before the transfer), or the right of salary increment as defined for academic rank.
4.11.14 Persons who have lost or who have never held General Faculty status and who are appointed assistant or associate dean are not members of the General Faculty and shall not have department, college or General Faculty voting privileges, nor shall they be counted for apportionment of the Faculty Senate. #20-21-36
4.12.10 Special Status Appointments. The rights and privileges of faculty status, excepting the rights of tenure and of election to the Faculty Senate, and with other stated exceptions, shall be extended to the following categories (4.12.11-12): [ Administrative January 2013 ]

4.12.11 Administrative. The Vice Presidents and the directors of major University divisions, with the further exception of the right of salary increment as defined for faculty ranks. [ Administrative January 2013 ]
4.12.12 Coaching positions shall be based on appointment by the Director of Athletics and shall be related to the coaching of intercollegiate athletics. If coaching appointees are assigned a part-time responsibility for teaching or research within the University, they shall be separately contracted for such services. [ Administrative January 2013 ]
4.13.10 Clinical Faculty. These non tenure-track faculty shall be appointed in the College of Pharmacy, the College of Nursing, and other colleges and departments requiring clinical training to contribute to the instruction, practice scholarship, supervision, and service in a clinical setting. 4.20.10 Organization of the General Faculty. The President of the University shall be the presiding officer of the General Faculty. #20-21-36
4.20.11 The other officers of the faculty shall be a secretary, a parliamentarian, a marshal and assistant marshals, appointed by the President.

4.30.10 The Faculty Senate. The General Faculty, through legislative act on May 12, 1960, authorized the establishment of a Faculty Senate as its agent to conduct in a responsible and efficient manner the business assigned to faculty jurisdiction by law, the President, or by the Rhode Island Board of Trustees (now the URI Board of Trustees). It was the intent that the faculty delegate to the Senate all powers of the faculty, with the exception of those stipulated in this chapter, that are specifically delegated elsewhere, so long as the Senate shall represent the will of the faculty. Approval of the Senate Constitution and By-Laws was granted by the former Rhode Island Board of Trustees on November 1, 1961. #21-22-6 #October 20, 2022 Informational Report

4.32.10 Jurisdiction of College Faculties. The General Faculty delegates to each college faculty jurisdiction over matters primarily of interest only to that college, such as: distribution of units for entrance requirements among secondary school subjects; the curricula of the college within limits of the general policies prescribed by the Faculty Senate; action concerning petitions for changes in prescribed courses of study, presented by individual students enrolled in the college; recommendations to the General Faculty concerning the granting of degrees to students enrolled in the college; and decisions concerning the scholastic standing of students enrolled in the college, through the college’s Scholastic Standing Committee, to which this matter is delegated. #20-21-36
4.32.11 Questions of jurisdiction as to the powers of the General Faculty (or its representative body, the Faculty Senate) and the faculties of several colleges shall be referred to the President. Appeals from the President’s ruling shall be decided by the General Faculty.

4.40.10 The General Faculty shall meet at the beginning of the academic year for an address by the President, at other times determined by the President or when a meeting is requested in writing by 25 percent of the faculty. The faculty shall regulate its own procedure. #20-21-36
4.40.11 The General Faculty shall act upon the recommendations made by the several college faculties and by the Graduate Faculty for the granting of degrees in course to those who have fulfilled the requirements for the appropriate degrees. 4.40.12 Attendance at meetings of the General Faculty is expected. One-fourth of the membership or a quorum of the Faculty Senate shall constitute a quorum of the General Faculty. #20-21-36 #24-25-20

4.40.14 Meetings of the faculty shall be conducted in accordance with American Institute of Parliamentarians Standard Code of Parliamentary Procedure. #18-19-31

4.40.15 The General Faculty shall vote on amendments to the Constitution of the Senate as provided in Article VII of the Constitution. #20-21-36
4.40.16 The General Faculty shall retain the power to review at any time decisions made by the Faculty Senate. Upon petition signed by 10 percent of the members of the General Faculty, a referendum shall be conducted as provided in Article II, Paragraph 6, of the Constitution. #20-21-36

4.50.10 College Faculties. Faculty members assigned to a college of the University shall constitute the faculty of that college. A democratic procedure in the conduct of department meetings is essential. The chairperson shall be responsible for keeping all members fully informed on matters of concern to the department. #21-22-6

4.60.11 Among the matters discussed in department meetings should be the advisability of introduction of new courses, especially those that give members opportunities for developing specific interests, provided, however, that more essential courses are not dropped or neglected.
4.60.12 Voting on matters which require approval of the Faculty Senate shall be the privilege of all full-time tenure track faculty from their effective date of hire and the privilege of full-time non-tenure track faculty who have been employed as such for at least one year. #14-15–15 #24-25-20
4.60.13 The use of department funds shall be open to discussion in department meetings. #23-24-4

4.60.14 The chairperson shall be responsible for informing department members of the opportunities for teaching in the Summer Session, or special courses elsewhere. The chairperson shall consult with the Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success to determine what courses will meet student demand and accelerate degree completion in Summer and Winter J-Term sessions. However, no new faculty member shall be engaged with definite or implied guarantees of such teaching, nor shall current faculty members be promised such teaching on a continuing basis. #18-19-34 #24-25-20 #25-26-CBUM-03

4.60.15 The recommendation to the Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success for teachers of Summer Session courses within the department or program shall be discussed by the voting faculty members of the department or program in question in a department or program meeting. It is often desirable to assign summer courses to persons who teach those courses during the regular school year. It should be the aim of department chairpersons to distribute these appointments as fairly as possible among department members who are interested in and qualified for the positions available. However, it is a policy of the University that a number of visiting faculty members shall be engaged for the Summer Session and department chairpersons shall staff their summer programs with this policy in mind. #18-19-34 ; Informational Report 2022-2023-6

4.60.20 Joint Appointments . A faculty member may be appointed to a professorial position in more than one department (usually not more than two departments) upon the recommendation of the departments and dean (deans, if more than one college is involved) subject to the approval of the Provost. Such appointments may be either unlimited or limited.
4.60.21 Persons holding unlimited joint appointments may participate fully in all activities of the departments including teaching, research, service, and student supervision. They shall have full voting privileges in the departments. The conditions of tenured status as well as the person or persons responsible for conducting annual reviews will be specified in writing and agreed to by the departments, deans, and the individual at the time of the initial appointment.

4.60.22 Persons holding limited joint appointments may participate in the teaching, research, or service programs of the second department. The faculty member with a limited joint appointment shall have voting rights only on issues related to the program or curriculum in which they are involved. They are not involved in peer-review. Any other privileges and obligations associated with the limited appointment in the second department shall be determined by mutual agreement and must be specified in writing at the time the appointment is approved.

The Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree.
The interdisciplinary degree in Criminology and Criminal Justice provides students with a wide range of course options so that students may tailor their learning to their educational and professional interests.
Our purpose is to empower our graduates to meaningfully consider, contribute to, and reimagine discourses and decisions about crime and justice.
The CCJ Department does this by making intentional choices about our work and remaining committed to continual professional growth and community building.
The program requires 30-49 credits in the major including CCJ/SOC 230(H) (with a grade of C or better), CCJ/PSC 274(H) (with a grade of C or better), and one of three capstone classes: CCJ 403, CCJ 410 or CCJ/PSC 476.
Students must select one research methods course from the following: ECN 306, PSC 310, PSY 200, or SOC 301.

Students are required to take six elective courses selected from the following two areas: criminology electives – AAF 230; CCJ 200 (approved topics), 334, 370, 400 (approved topics), 403, 410, 450, 476; AAF/HIS 366; PHL 318; PSY 254, 466; SOC 420; criminal justice electives – AAF 230; CCJ 200 (approved topics), 280, 285, 290,,, 332, 333, 381 (must be taken in combination with CHM 391 and/or ITR 305 for a total of 3 credits to count as 1 elective class), 456, 480, 490, 400 (approved topics), 403, 410, 476; CHM 391 (must either be repeated 3 times or taken in combination with CCJ 381 and/or ITR 305 for a total of 3 credits to count as 1 elective class); CCJ/HIS 361, AAF/HIS 366; ITR 305 (must be taken in combination with CHM 391 and/or CCJ 381 for a total of 3 credits to count as 1 elective class) PSC 334, 371, 388, 472; PSY 465; SOC 303.
At least two courses must be taken from each elective area and no more than four courses can be taken in either area.
All electives must be a minimum of 3 credits.
While CCJ 403, 410, and CCJ/PSC 476 are each capstone classes and electives, students may not use the same course to count as both a capstone and an elective class.

When appropriate, and by permission of the Department Chair, students may substitute internship credit (SOC 477, PSC 375/376, PSY 305, or GWS 300) or independent study credit (CCJ 485, SOC 498/499, PSC 455/456, PSY 489, or GWS 450) for one of their elective courses listed above.
No more than 3 credits may be used toward the major from internship or independent study.
Internal transfers into the CCJ major form a different major, or students wishing to add the CCJ major to their current major, must have a minimum 2.50 GPA.
A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.
At least 30 of these credits must be in courses at the 300-level or above.
In order to transfer into the criminology and criminal justice B.A. program from University College for Academic Success, a student must have completed at least 24 credits and have an earned a minimum of a 2.0 GPA.
